title: Reciprocal translocation t(8;14)
clinical_history: A 12-year-old patient presents with a rapidly enlarging jaw mass. Biopsy shows a high-grade B-cell lymphoma with a starry-sky pattern. Tumor cytogenetics is requested.
plain_language_interpretation: A male karyotype with 46 chromosomes and a reciprocal translocation between 8q24 and 14q32, corresponding to MYC::IGH rearrangement.
explanation: Burkitt lymphoma classically carries t(8;14)(q24;q32), placing MYC at 8q24 under control of the IGH enhancer at 14q32. Variant translocations involve IGK t(2;8) or IGL t(8;22). Follicular lymphoma is associated with t(14;18)(q32;q21) (IGH::BCL2) and mantle cell lymphoma with t(11;14)(q13;q32) (IGH::CCND1); those are different breakpoints and partner chromosomes. This teaching case uses the classic t(8;14) form.
hints: This is a lymphoid neoplasm of childhood or adolescence, not a myeloproliferative neoplasm.
MYC is at 8q24; IGH is at 14q32. The classic Burkitt translocation joins those two bands.
Chromosomes in a translocation are listed in numerical order: t(8;14), not t(14;8).
